reason: Section 5 authorizes the Commission board to appoint officers and designate the Chief Compliance Officer, requires identification cards, and permits designation of officers appointed by other governments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Appointment, identification, and interjurisdictional designation of occupational health and safety officers
proposedGroups.reason: Section 5 authorizes the Commission board to appoint officers and designate the Chief Compliance Officer, requires identification cards, and permits designation of officers appointed by other governments.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how occupational health and safety officers and the Chief Compliance Officer are appointed, identified and designated for interjurisdictional work.

reason: Section 5.1 gives the Chief Compliance Officer authority to delegate powers, duties, authority or discretion to another occupational health and safety officer on terms and conditions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Delegation by the Chief Compliance Officer

evidenceText: to another occupational health and safety officer

proposedGroups.reason: Section 5.1 gives the Chief Compliance Officer authority to delegate powers, duties, authority or discretion to another occupational health and safety officer on terms and conditions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what the Chief Compliance Officer may delegate and to whom.

reason: Section 6 permits the Commission to designate technical experts to accompany an officer into a place of employment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Technical experts accompanying officers
proposedGroups.reason: Section 6 permits the Commission to designate technical experts to accompany an officer into a place of employment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who may designate technical experts and the inspection setting in which they may accompany officers.

reason: Section 7 authorizes an inquiry under the Inquiries Act at the Commission request and requires commissioners to record and report evidence, findings and proceedings to the Commission for submission to the Lieutenant-Governor in Council.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Commission-requested inquiries into occupational health and safety
proposedGroups.reason: Section 7 authorizes an inquiry under the Inquiries Act at the Commission request and requires commissioners to record and report evidence, findings and proceedings to the Commission for submission to the Lieutenant-Governor in Council.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how an occupational health and safety inquiry is initiated and reported.

reason: Section 8 requires employers with 20 or more employees regularly employed in the Province to establish a written safety policy in consultation with employees, state responsibilities, keep it at each place of employment, and make it available to officers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Employer safety policy for workplaces with 20 or more employees
proposedGroups.reason: Section 8 requires employers with 20 or more employees regularly employed in the Province to establish a written safety policy in consultation with employees, state responsibilities, keep it at each place of employment, and make it available to officers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an employer must have a written safety policy and what it must cover and where it must be kept.

reason: Section 8.1 has one study topic for the required contents of a written health and safety program and another for annual review and access to the program and records.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Required contents of employer health and safety programs
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 8.1(1) requires a written program for employers with 20 or more employees and lists training, work procedures, hazard identification, investigations, record management and monitoring contents.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the required elements of a written health and safety program for employers with 20 or more employees.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Annual review and access to health and safety program records
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 8.1(2) and (3) require annual review with the committee or representative and require access to the program and records for the committee, representative, employees and Commission.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the annual review and access obligations for health and safety programs and records.

reason: Section 8.2 defines new employee and requires position-specific orientation and training before work, permits orientation only where prior training is documented, lists orientation topics, and requires records for at least three years.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: New employee orientation, prior training recognition, required topics, and records
proposedGroups.reason: Section 8.2 defines new employee and requires position-specific orientation and training before work, permits orientation only where prior training is documented, lists orientation topics, and requires records for at least three years.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who counts as a new employee and what orientation, training, topic coverage and recordkeeping the employer must provide.

reason: Section 9 is the core employer-duty provision and separates general compliance duties from specific hazard, information, supervision and equipment duties, plus inspection-program cooperation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: General employer duties to protect employees and ensure compliance
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 9(1) requires every employer to take reasonable precautions for employee health and safety, comply with the Act, regulations and orders, and ensure employee compliance.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the general employer duties to protect employee health and safety and ensure compliance with the Act, regulations and orders.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Employer duties for safe systems, hazards, information, supervision, and protective equipment
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 9(2) lists specific duties for safe systems and equipment, monthly inspections, hazard familiarization, information, instruction, training, competent and sufficient supervision, protective equipment, and cooperation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the specific employer duties for workplace systems, hazards, inspections, training, supervision, protective equipment and cooperation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Employer inspection program and sharing of inspection results
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 9(3) requires the employer to develop the monthly inspection program with the committee or health and safety representative and share each inspection result.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must help develop the workplace inspection program and who receives inspection results.

reason: Section 9.1 states supervisors general reasonable-precaution, compliance, employee-compliance and cooperation duties, and adds specific duties to acquaint employees with hazards and provide necessary information and instruction.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Supervisor duties for health, safety, compliance, hazards, information, and instruction
proposedGroups.reason: Section 9.1 states supervisors general reasonable-precaution, compliance, employee-compliance and cooperation duties, and adds specific duties to acquaint employees with hazards and provide necessary information and instruction.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the general and specific occupational health and safety duties imposed on supervisors.

reason: Section 10 requires every contractor and sub-contractor to comply with the Act, regulations and orders, and to take every reasonable precaution for health and safety at project sites for which they are responsible.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Contractor and sub-contractor compliance and project-site safety duties
proposedGroups.reason: Section 10 requires every contractor and sub-contractor to comply with the Act, regulations and orders, and to take every reasonable precaution for health and safety at project sites for which they are responsible.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the compliance and project-site safety duties of contractors and sub-contractors.

reason: Section 10.1 requires a contracting employer directing one or more employers at a place of employment to ensure, as far as reasonably practicable, that each employer complies, requires the contracting employer own compliance, and excludes private homes.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Contracting employer duty to ensure employer compliance
proposedGroups.reason: Section 10.1 requires a contracting employer directing one or more employers at a place of employment to ensure, as far as reasonably practicable, that each employer complies, requires the contracting employer own compliance, and excludes private homes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when a contracting employer must ensure other employers comply with the Act and the private-home exclusion.

reason: Section 11 requires every owner of a place of employment or part of it to comply with the Act, regulations and orders, and to take every reasonable precaution for persons accessing or using the place.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Owner compliance and safety duties for places of employment

evidenceText: Every owner of a place of employment

proposedGroups.reason: Section 11 requires every owner of a place of employment or part of it to comply with the Act, regulations and orders, and to take every reasonable precaution for persons accessing or using the place.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the compliance and reasonable-precaution duties imposed on owners of places of employment.

reason: Section 12 lists employee duties to comply, act safely, report known hazards, use required protective equipment, consult and cooperate with committees or representatives, and cooperate with enforcement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Employee duties for compliance, safe conduct, hazard reporting, protective equipment, consultation, and cooperation
proposedGroups.reason: Section 12 lists employee duties to comply, act safely, report known hazards, use required protective equipment, consult and cooperate with committees or representatives, and cooperate with enforcement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the health and safety duties imposed on every employee.

reason: Section 13 requires suppliers to take reasonable precautions that supplied tools, equipment, machines, devices or agents are safe and compliant, provide safe-use directions, and ensure required labelling.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Supplier duties for safe products, directions, compliance, and labelling

evidenceText: reasonably safe when used as directed

proposedGroups.reason: Section 13 requires suppliers to take reasonable precautions that supplied tools, equipment, machines, devices or agents are safe and compliant, provide safe-use directions, and ensure required labelling.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the occupational health and safety duties of suppliers for safe products, directions and labelling.

reason: Section 14 contains distinct committee topics: when a committee must be established and how it is composed, how meetings and records work, and how unresolved matters reach an officer.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Non-project-site committee establishment, composition, representation, and co-chairs
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections exclude project sites, require committees for employers with 20 or more employees at a place of employment, and set size, equal representation, Chief Compliance Officer size-setting and co-chair rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a non-project-site joint health and safety committee is required and how its membership and co-chairs are determined.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Committee meetings, minutes, posting, retention, and Commission access
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require monthly meetings, approved minutes, posting names and recent minutes, retaining signed minutes for three years and making them available to the Commission.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the meeting, minute, posting, retention and Commission-access duties for a committee.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Officer resolution of committee deadlock
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 14(13) requires a committee that cannot agree on a health and safety matter to call an officer to resolve the problem.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a joint health and safety committee must do when it cannot agree on a health and safety matter.

reason: Section 14.01 allows the Commission to approve organizations to deliver prescribed educational programs, the program content and duration, and other terms and conditions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Commission approval of organizations and educational programs
proposedGroups.reason: Section 14.01 allows the Commission to approve organizations to deliver prescribed educational programs, the program content and duration, and other terms and conditions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what the Commission may approve for prescribed educational programs.

reason: Section 14.1 excludes project sites, requires designated committee members to attend prescribed educational programs or do so within twelve months, preserves existing members, allows recommended voluntary attendance, permits Commission leave orders, and protects pay and benefits.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Training and paid leave for non-project-site committee members
proposedGroups.reason: Section 14.1 excludes project sites, requires designated committee members to attend prescribed educational programs or do so within twelve months, preserves existing members, allows recommended voluntary attendance, permits Commission leave orders, and protects pay and benefits.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the training, leave, Commission order, pay and benefits rules for non-project-site committee members.

reason: Section 14.2 has separate project-site committee operating rules and separate rules adapting section 15 and assigning contractor posting duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: General operation and records of project-site joint health and safety committees
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections apply to project-site committees, set co-chair election, continuation until work completes, monthly meetings, minutes, contractor copies, record retention and officer resolution of deadlock.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how project-site joint health and safety committees operate, meet, keep records and resolve deadlocks.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Section 15 adaptations and contractor posting duties for project-site committees
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14.2(7) and (8) apply section 15 with specified wording changes and require the responsible contractor to post committee member names and recent minutes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify how section 15 applies to project-site committees and what the contractor must post at the project site.
